chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The intention of the Believer is better than his deed, and the intention of the disbeliever is more evil than his deed, and every deed is performed upon its intention'.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of intention (niyyah) in Islamic ethics according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, establishes the principle that the spiritual value of an action is derived primarily from the sincerity of the heart, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence and ethics. It highlights that for the believer, even a modest act performed with pure intent holds greater merit than the same act performed by a disbeliever, while also affirming the general prophetic maxim that deeds are judged by intentions. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on internal conviction (iman) as the root of external practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The intention of the Believer is better than his deed, and the intention of the disbeliever is more evil than his deed, and every deed is performed upon its intention’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘The intention of the believer is better than his deeds, and the intention of the unbeliever is more wicked than his deeds. Everyone acts according to his intention.’”
